Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the city's webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, and Amazon Fire devices
using a free app called Screenweave and choosing “Glendale TV” from the menu. Meetings are also
archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas. Call (818) 548-4013 for
program schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City Clerk's Office.
For public comments and questions during the meeting, call (818) 937-8100. Public comments on a
specific agenda item will be taken when that agenda item is discussed. If you have any question about
matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the City Clerk at (818) 548-2090
during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents related
to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and
are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E. Broadway, RM
110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.

  July 7, 2022
  Date

91206 to consider the following item(s) of business, to wit;

6. OATH OF OFFICE TO NEWLY ELECTED CITY OFFICERS:
  Senator Anthony Portantino administered the Oath of Office.

  COUNCIL MEMBERS – Elen Asatryan, Dan Brotman, Ara Najarian
  CITY CLERK – Suzie Abajian
  CITY TREASURER – Rafi Manoukian

7. NEW COUNCIL IS SEATED

8. COMMENTS BY NEWLY-ELECTED OFFICIALS
  City Treasurer Rafi Manoukian congratulated the newly-elected officials, thanked his family
  and friends for their support, commended the candidates who participated in the election
  process, and thanked the voters for voting in this election and entrusting him to serve as City
  Treasurer for the next four years.

  City Clerk Suzie Abajian was honored to receive the support of the voters in Glendale and
  thanked them for entrusting her with this very important position. She stated that the clerk is
  the purveyor of the democratic process within city government. She looks forward to serving
  our city for the next four years. She thanked everyone who supported her campaign, including
  her committed team and her family. She was elated to see more women elected to city
  government and was overjoyed to be part of this welcomed change to the city. She revisited
  07 12 22

 her campaign promises including transparency, access and voter empowerment, the
importance of good information governance, open data initiatives, modernizing city platforms
for sharing information, and voter outreach in culturally and linguistically responsive ways. She
will work collaboratively with residents to make the city more transparent, accessible, and
inclusive.

Councilmember Ara Najarian thanked his family, voters, several organizations, and agencies
that supported him. He thanked the other candidates who ran and gave their all. He
mentioned that he is the longest-serving councilmember in Glendale and will bring his
decades of experience, institutional memory, and knowledge to the city. He stated that this
election was different from previous ones. He critiqued political partisanship, voting systems,
touch screens, and the long wait from the County to tabulate the votes. He stated that his
election had great significance for the city because of his chairmanship of the Metro Board. He
promised to be free from outside influences such as partisan dogma. He will support public
safety, traffic and pedestrian safety, bicycle safety, and law enforcement. He will oppose
bringing marijuana dispensaries and related marijuana production sites. He discussed the
importance of having green space and affordable housing in South Glendale. He will make
sure that the City will have the electrical power that it needs to keep the lights on. He would
like to create a new and bigger aquatic facility. He spoke about improvements and funding for
public transportation and bike lanes in the city.

Councilmember Elen Asatryan congratulated the newly-elected officials. She was grateful to
her team and supporters who helped her get elected. She thanked her family as well. She
hopes to build a collegial atmosphere with colleagues, staff, and residents. Her top priorities: a
positive culture in City Hall, focusing on the needs of South Glendale, better communication
and outreach, safer streets, green spaces, affordable housing, sustainability, arts, public
transit, walkable streets, and bike lanes. She would like to see diversity celebrated through
dynamic arts, entertainment and cultural programs. She would like to create innovative
programs for recovery and support for small businesses and bring Glendale into the digital
age for efficiency by modernizing the permitting process. Ms. Asatryan is also focused on
preserving the beauty of the city’s unique neighborhoods and historic structures. She looks
forward to building a more sustainable Glendale by cleaning-up and finding alternatives for the
Scholl Canyon Landfill and Grayson Power Plant. She would like to add youth seats to all
boards and commissions and to bring back the powers that are stripped from the Women’s
Commission. She stated that her election meant a lot to young women and girls and she looks
forward to help pave the way to create greater opportunities for them to get civically engaged.
She will proactively address homelessness and mental health and ensure that the police and
fire departments have the resources they need to keep the city safe. Lastly, she indicated that
her end goal is to serve the public and leave this city better than it was found. She asked staff,
in return, to come to work with an open heart. She looks forward to our collective work ahead
in making Glendale truly a model city in which we can live, work, and play.

Councilmember Dan Brotman thanked Mayor Kassakhian for encouraging him to get involved
and participate in city government. He thanked several elected officials and individuals for their
mentorship. He also thanked his family for their love and support and everyone who
contributed, volunteered, and shared his vision for a more sustainable, innovative, forward-
looking, and equitable Glendale. He spoke about his 10-point plan which included
environmental sustainability, housing, transportation and walkability, arts and culture equity,
quality of life, business recovery, urban design and development, and the city’s financial health.
He also advocated for an immediate decision on the Grayson Power Plant and meeting the
city’s needs in the upcoming decade through developing reliable/clean energy alternatives,

   retiring our fossil fuel assets and getting 100% clean and renewable energy by 2035. He spoke
  about reducing greenhouse gas emissions by building electrification, increasing charging
  infrastructure, electrification of the city’s vehicle fleet, electrification of landscape equipment
  and confronting waste management challenges by reducing single-use plastics, encouraging
  reusables for dine-in restaurant services, and dealing with the closure of the Scholl Canyon
  Landfill. He wanted to explore solutions for keeping the community safe in the more extreme
  heat, recurring water shortages, heightened fire risks, etc. Mr. Brotman would like to see the
  renovation of Rockhaven, the Verdugo Wash Project, the construction of the Armenian-
  American Museum, and redoing of the Artsakh Paseo. He indicated he wanted to develop new
  town centers in the areas around Adams Square Mini-Park and Glendale Community College,
  and park space when Scholl Canyon Landfill closes. He stated that there is a looming
  challenge with the unfunded pension liabilities and incremental adjustments are needed on
  both the revenue and cost sides to avoid major lay-offs and service impacts. He would also like
  to see a jazz club in Glendale.
